newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa bean exports still strong in July.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa bean exports still strong in July.

text.p: Ivory Coast's cocoa bean exports fell to 48,566 tonnes in July from 83,314 tonnes in June but they were still very strong for the month, official data show.
Exports in July last year amounted to 18,232 tonnes and in 1993/94 they were 17,376 tonnes.
Cumulative exports for the first 10 months of 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) were 1,054,027 tonnes tonnes against 737,295 tonnes tonnes in the same period of 1994/95.
The figures showed Abidjan handled 41,051 tonnes of beans last month and San Pedro, Ivory Coast's second port, shipped 7,515 tonnes.
The main destination was Amsterdam, which took 22,075 tonnes. The United States received 1,522 tonnes.
Cumulative October-to-July shipments to the Netherlands were 431,243 tonnes and exports to North America were 204,117 tonnes.
This compares with 369,412 tonnes and 18,374 tonnes respectively in the same period of 1994/95.

Trade sources said the big rise in exports to North America was mainly due to a cut in Ivorian shipping rates at the start of this season which made it cost effective to ship cocoa there directly rather than sending it via Amsterdam.
Dutch warehousing sources have nonetheless described this as their best year ever as cocoa has poured into Amsterdam to be delivered against the squeezed September contract in London.

Ivory Coast has been a ready supplier of both the European and American markets. Its 1995/96 crop is forecast at a record 1.2 million tonnes, about a third more than the previous best crop in 1994/95. --David Gault, Abidjan Newsroom +225 21 90 90
